def: The single certificate that records who owns a building and the land-use right beneath it. It replaced the old 房产证 and 土地证 pair. Read four fields: nature of right, use, term end date, registered area.
The main tax a buyer pays at registration: 1% up to 140m² for a first or second home, 1.5–2% above, 3% for commercial stock or a third home.
Around 5.3% on resale, generally exempt where the seller has held the property for two years or more. Legally the seller's tax, often negotiated onto the buyer.
On sale, typically 1% of price or 20% of the gain. Exempt where the property has been the seller's only home for five years or more.
The condition that exempts a seller from individual income tax: held five years or more and the seller's only residential property. A standard negotiation term.
An account held jointly by buyer, seller and bank, released only when named documents are produced. The mechanism that stops a deposit disappearing with a seller.
The step that enters the sale into the housing authority's system, locking the unit against a second sale and formally testing your eligibility.
A commitment payment, usually 1–5% of price, against a written deposit agreement. Its refund conditions decide who carries the risk.
The buyer's equity contribution, paid into escrow after contract registration. For foreign buyers, typically 40–50% of price because loan-to-value is capped lower.
The remainder released when ownership transfers, normally held in escrow until the new certificate is issued.
What you actually acquire over state-owned land, for a fixed term: 70 years residential, 50 institutional, 40 commercial. The clock starts at the land grant, not at your purchase.
40- or 50-year units sold as apartments. Commercial utilities, no school catchment, higher taxes, shorter mortgages — and generally closed to foreign individual buyers.
The administrative mapping of address to school place. It drives large price premiums and is repriced by policy, not by the market.
Municipal limits on who may buy and how many. For foreign nationals the effective limit is one self-use home, in the city of employment, after a qualifying year.
The police-station registration a foreign national must complete after moving in, and after any address change. Hotels do it for you; private leases do not.
Charged per square metre per month, roughly ¥3–15. On 120m² at ¥8 that is ¥11,520 a year — a sixth of the rent on a 1.7% yield.
A one-off contribution at purchase, around 2–3% of price on new homes, held for major building repairs. Not a fee you can recover on sale.
A legal freeze on a property, usually from litigation or debt. A sealed unit cannot transfer. This is what a registry search is looking for.
A registered charge over the property, normally a bank loan. It must be discharged before transfer; a promise to release it later is not the same thing.
The registration step at which the property becomes yours. The balance in escrow is released against the new certificate, not against a promise.
The permission a developer needs before selling unbuilt units. It is building- and stage-specific; paying without one leaves your money unprotected.
The benchmark rate Chinese mortgages are priced against, with a spread, and repriced annually. Compare total cost, not the headline rate.
Bare shell means no flooring, kitchen or bathroom — the common state of new builds. Fitted out means a specification you should read line by line, because it moves.
The portion of the registered area allocated to corridors, lifts and common space, commonly 20–30%. It is why a 100m² unit may feel like 75m².
